skill.name: workflow-orchestration-patterns

skill.summary: Plan reliable Temporal workflows with clear activity boundaries, compensation patterns, and replay-safe state management.

content.value_statement: Distributed workflows fail when orchestration, external calls, and retries are mixed without clear rules. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Temporal patterns for durable workflows, sagas, callbacks, and deterministic state management.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to model logic as a Temporal workflow or an activity.
Outlines saga compensation, entity workflow, fan-out, fan-in, and async callback patterns.
Lists workflow determinism rules, including allowed Temporal time and random APIs.
Describes retry policies, non-retryable errors, idempotency keys, and activity heartbeats.
Summarizes operational concerns such as worker scaling, task queues, and monitoring signals.
limitations: Does not generate complete production Temporal projects by itself.
Does not validate a live Temporal cluster or worker configuration.
Examples are conceptual and may need language-specific SDK adaptation.
Does not replace security, data consistency, or payments compliance review.

use_cases.title: Plan a Payment Saga
use_cases.description: Map payment, inventory, and fulfillment steps with compensation tasks before implementation.

use_cases.title: Model Entity Lifecycles
use_cases.description: Design long-lived workflows for carts, accounts, inventory, or approvals that receive signals and expose queries.

use_cases.title: Review Temporal Reliability
use_cases.description: Check workflow boundaries, idempotency, retries, timeouts, and replay safety before launch.

prompt_templates.title: Classify Workflow Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the workflow-orchestration-patterns skill. Classify these steps as Temporal workflows or activities, and explain each boundary: [paste process].

prompt_templates.title: Design a Saga
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the workflow-orchestration-patterns skill. Create a saga plan for [business process]. Include forward steps, compensation steps, idempotency needs, and non-retryable errors.

prompt_templates.title: Scale Fan-Out Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the workflow-orchestration-patterns skill. Design a bounded fan-out and fan-in workflow for [task volume]. Include child workflows, retry policies, heartbeats, and monitoring signals.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Determinism and Versioning
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the workflow-orchestration-patterns skill. Review this Temporal design for determinism, replay compatibility, versioning, activity boundaries, payload limits, and operational risks: [paste design].

output_examples.input: A checkout workflow reserves inventory, charges payment, and creates shipment.
output: Workflow boundary: the workflow coordinates the order and tracks state.
Activities: reserve inventory, charge payment, and create shipment because they touch external systems.
Compensations: release inventory, refund payment, and cancel shipment in reverse order.

output_examples.input: A user approval process waits two days for a manager response.
output: Pattern: async callback with a workflow signal.
The workflow sends the approval request and waits for a signal or timeout.
Use an activity to send the request and classify invalid approvals as non-retryable.

output_examples.input: A workflow processes one million records through external enrichment calls.
output: Use bounded fan-out with child workflows instead of one oversized workflow.
Put enrichment calls in activities with timeouts, retry limits, and heartbeats.
Monitor pending workflow counts, activity failures, and retry backoff behavior.

best_practices: Keep orchestration in workflows and all external calls in activities.
Register saga compensation before each forward step executes.
Define activity timeouts, retry limits, heartbeats, and idempotency keys.
anti_patterns: Calling external APIs, databases, file systems, or network services directly from workflow code.
Using system time, random values, global state, or non-deterministic libraries in workflows.
Letting activities retry forever without classifying permanent business errors.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps teams design Temporal workflows that survive failures and preserve state across long-running processes.

faq.question: Does it write runnable Temporal code?
faq.answer: It focuses on architecture patterns and review guidance. Generated code still needs SDK-specific implementation and testing.

faq.question: Can it help with distributed transactions?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains saga compensation and reverse-order rollback for multi-step business processes.

faq.question: How does it handle external services?
faq.answer: It recommends putting API calls, database writes, messages, and file operations inside activities.

faq.question: Is this only for Temporal?
faq.answer: The examples target Temporal, but many durability and orchestration principles apply to similar workflow engines.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. It is written as guidance that these tools can use during design and code review.
